hero.headline: TSMC Commits Additional $100 Billion for US Chip Production
hero.teaser: The Taiwanese semiconductor manufacturer has raised its total US investment commitment to $265 billion.
hero.body:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company announced it will invest another $100 billion to expand its chip production operations in the United States. The pledge increases the company's total commitment to its US facilities to $265 billion, marking one of the largest foreign investments in American manufacturing.

TSMC said the expansion will create high-tech, high-paying jobs as part of its fast-growing operations in Arizona. The company manufactures advanced semiconductors used in everything from smartphones to artificial intelligence systems.

cards.headline: US and Iran exchange strikes for fifth consecutive day
cards.body:
The United States and Iran conducted sustained military strikes against each other for the fifth straight day, with explosions reported across Iran overnight following attacks from neighboring Gulf states in the region.

The US military completed an additional round of strikes on July 14 at 10pm Eastern Time, with fighter aircraft, drones, and naval vessels launching precision munitions during a seven-hour operation. US Central Command said the strikes targeted dozens of military positions near the strait of Hormuz and Iranian coastal areas, including missile and drone sites, naval capabilities, and coastal defense systems. The military said these attacks were designed to further degrade Iran's ability to threaten commercial shipping.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps responded by targeting what it described as command-and-control, logistics, fuel and military equipment facilities belonging to the US Fifth Fleet in Bahrain. The Guards said this was in response to US actions in the Indian Ocean and efforts to control the strait of Hormuz and restrict shipping routes. They warned that if Washington sought to block the region's oil and gas exports by controlling maritime routes, other export routes serving US and allied interests could also be closed, stating regional energy exports would be "for everyone or for no one."

Iran's revolutionary guards also claimed they attacked Kuwait's Mina Abdullah facility and destroyed a US military logistics center. The Iranian army said it targeted US military facilities at Azraq base in Jordan for a second time. Kuwait reported that its air defenses were intercepting Iranian attack drones, and sirens sounded in Bahrain following the attacks.

President Trump threatened to escalate the conflict further, telling Fox News: "Next week comes the power plants, next week comes the bridges, unless they get to the table and negotiate." However, Trump backtracked on an earlier threat to heavily tax ships passing through the strait of Hormuz.

Despite the military escalation, a top Iranian official indicated some openness to dialogue. Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said the US decision to renew a naval blockade "has, in a way, dismantled the Islamabad memorandum," referring to an interim deal signed in mid-June that included a 60-day timeline to negotiate an agreement on Iran's nuclear program. However, talks have stalled as fighting over the strait intensified.

US Central Command commander Admiral Brad Cooper said Iran had intentionally targeted civilians by attacking seven commercial ships in the past week, resulting in nearly a dozen civilian crew members killed, missing, or injured.

The US Treasury also imposed new sanctions targeting Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani's network, which the department said is a major force behind Iran's oil exports and has expanded into global containerized shipping and commodities trading.

This represents the longest sustained direct military confrontation between the two countries in recent memory, raising international concerns about wider regional conflict and disruption to critical shipping lanes and global energy markets.

cards.headline: Canadian wildfire smoke triggers air quality alerts across Northeast and Great Lakes
cards.body:
Smoke from Canadian wildfires has moved into the Northeast and Great Lakes regions, prompting air quality alerts across multiple states. Pennsylvania activated a Code Red air quality alert as hazy skies appeared over cities from New York to Philadelphia. The smoke created conditions similar to previous wildfire seasons that have affected millions of Americans.

Air quality officials issued warnings for residents in the New York City tri-state area, where the smoke returned after affecting the region in previous fire seasons. Philadelphia and surrounding communities also fell under air quality alerts as the smoke spread southward. Weather patterns carried the particulates across the border, reducing visibility and degrading air quality readings to levels considered dangerous for sensitive populations. The Great Lakes region experienced similar conditions as the smoke mass spread westward.

The smoke originated from active wildfires burning in Canada and drifted south into the United States. Health officials typically advise vulnerable populations including children, elderly residents, and people with respiratory conditions to limit outdoor activities during such events. The particulate matter in wildfire smoke can penetrate deep into lungs and cause breathing difficulties even in healthy individuals when concentrations reach elevated levels.

Recent research has revealed that wildfire smoke poses a greater threat to air quality than previously understood. A study published in Science found that since 2015, wildfires have reversed U.S. progress toward ozone air quality standards. Ground-level ozone is created when pollutants from cars, refineries and industrial sources react with sunlight. Wildfires emit carbon monoxide and other gases that contribute to ozone formation, with smoke spreading far beyond the fire source and leading to increasing ozone hundreds of miles away.

Despite regulated reductions in emissions, surface ozone levels have plateaued since 2015. The study links this plateau to wildfire emissions and found that the rise in ozone emissions is correlated with approximately 318 premature deaths each year since 2013. Researchers developed their findings by evaluating satellite data, EPA monitoring information, and meteorological data using deep learning models.

Wildfire smoke contains PM2.5, microscopic particles that can embed themselves deep in the lungs and enter the bloodstream. The pollutant has been linked to numerous health conditions and premature death. A 2024 study found that more than 50,000 people in California died prematurely over a decade due to exposure to toxic particles in wildfire smoke.

The alerts cover heavily populated urban centers home to tens of millions of Americans. Climate change has created conditions for more frequent and destructive wildfires across North America. Researchers note that mitigating climate change and implementing fire prevention measures can lead to improved air quality standards and potentially bring large benefits to public health.

cards.headline: Trump reverses DHS pause on ICE vehicle stops after two fatal shootings
cards.teaser: President Trump reversed a Department of Homeland Security decision to pause certain ICE vehicle stops, overruling his own agency after becoming angry about the.
cards.body:
President Trump reversed a Department of Homeland Security decision to pause certain ICE vehicle stops, overruling his own agency after becoming angry about the temporary measure. The DHS had announced the pause following two fatal shootings by ICE agents in recent weeks, with the intent to provide additional training to agents before resuming such operations.

Late Tuesday at the White House, Trump complained to advisers about the pause, according to reports. By Wednesday morning, he posted on Truth Social reversing the decision, leaving DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin and border czar Tom Homan to explain the abrupt change in policy.

The two fatal shootings that prompted the original pause involved immigrant fathers who were killed during ICE operations. Federal immigration agents involved in the recent shootings were not wearing body cameras, according to the agency. The DHS had earlier pledged to equip all immigration agents with body cameras, but months later that promise has not been fulfilled.

The reversal highlights tension between the White House and DHS over immigration enforcement operations. The original pause was intended as a temporary safety measure while agents received additional training on vehicle stop procedures. Trump's intervention means ICE agents will continue conducting vehicle stops without the planned training period.

The episode demonstrates how the recent fatal shootings have created pressure on the administration's immigration enforcement policies. The lack of body camera footage from either incident has made it difficult to establish complete accounts of what occurred during the confrontations that led to the deaths.

cards.headline: Lawmakers push for windfall tax on oil company profits since Iran war
cards.teaser: Some U.S. lawmakers want to tax excess oil company profits generated since the Iran war began and redistribute the revenue to lower-income Americans.
cards.body:
Higher oil prices following the start of the Iran war have resulted in substantial excess profits for oil companies. U.S. lawmakers are now pushing to impose a windfall profits tax on these earnings.

Supporters of the proposed tax want to redirect the revenue toward providing financial assistance to lower-income Americans struggling with elevated energy costs.

cards.headline: Federal immigration agents involved in fatal shootings lacked body cameras
cards.teaser: Two immigrant fathers were fatally shot by federal immigration agents in recent days, with none of the officers wearing body cameras despite a Department of Homeland Security pledge.
cards.body:
Federal immigration agents fatally shot two immigrant fathers in recent days. None of the officers involved in either shooting were wearing body cameras, according to the Department of Homeland Security.

The agency had previously pledged to equip all immigration agents with body cameras. That commitment has not yet been fulfilled, and the officers involved in the fatal incidents were not equipped with the devices at the time of the shootings.

cards.headline: Todd Blanche faces confirmation hearing for attorney general
cards.teaser: President Trump's nominee to lead the Justice Department answered questions from lawmakers about his relationship with Trump and potential investigations.
cards.body:
Todd Blanche appeared before the Senate Judiciary Committee on Wednesday for his confirmation hearing as President Trump's nominee to lead the Justice Department. The hearing revealed significant tensions as lawmakers from both parties questioned his close relationship with Trump and his role in the administration's recent decisions.

Blanche, who previously served as Trump's personal attorney and later as deputy attorney general, sought to distance himself from his close ties to the president. When asked directly by Louisiana Senator John Kennedy whether the two men were friends, Blanche initially said "I'm his lawyer" before correcting himself to "Was his lawyer." He later emphasized that his role as Trump's counsel did not make him a "yes man," and he claimed to have disagreed with the president on occasions, including on whether Trump was eligible to run for a third term.

The hearing focused on several controversial matters. Blanche faced pointed questioning about a settlement agreement between the Justice Department and Trump over a $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS. The deal included a $1.8 billion fund intended to compensate victims of alleged government weaponization, though Blanche acknowledged the term was not specifically defined. The agreement also granted Trump, his family, and his businesses immunity from tax audits. A federal judge on Monday criticized the arrangement as collusive. Facing bipartisan backlash, Blanche scrapped the fund.

Republican Senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis, both critical of the settlement, pressed Blanche during the hearing. Cornyn remained "undecided" on the nomination, while Tillis seemed to warm to Blanche after he stated that anyone who harmed law enforcement on January 6 should have been prosecuted. Tillis told Blanche he had done a good job.

Democratic Senator Dick Durbin raised concerns about the Justice Department's handling of files related to Jeffrey Epstein. Blanche acknowledged that the release contained "mistakes," including redaction errors. He defended the department's conduct but said he could not directly meet with Epstein survivors if they were represented by attorneys, though his staff would do so.

When asked by Democratic Senator Amy Klobuchar about whether armed agents would be deployed to polls in November, Blanche said he would "absolutely commit to following the law" but did not directly address the concern.

Blanche also defended FBI Director Kash Patel against reports about his drinking habits and use of the FBI's airplane. "I don't think he has any issues drinking," Blanche said. "I don't think there's any issues with morale there."

The confirmation faces a tight margin. Blanche cannot afford to lose a single Republican vote on the committee for his nomination to advance. Democratic Senator Cory Booker of New Jersey has publicly stated his opposition to the nomination.

cards.headline: Protests erupt in Ukrainian cities over defense minister dismissal
cards.teaser: Demonstrations broke out across Ukraine after President Zelensky removed Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov without explanation.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has dismissed Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov without providing a public explanation. The decision has triggered protests across the country's cities, with civil society groups and military members expressing strong opposition to the removal.

Fedorov, known for his tech-savvy approach, played a key role in Ukraine's drone warfare strategy against Russian forces. His departure comes as Ukraine navigates significant military developments, including new drone deals and efforts to secure Patriot missile licenses, adding to concerns about the timing of the leadership change.

cards.headline: Syria intercepts weapons shipment to Hezbollah from Iraq
cards.teaser: Syrian authorities seized weapons being smuggled from Iraq to Hezbollah, according to state news reports.
cards.body:
Syria stopped an attempt to smuggle weapons to Hezbollah from Iraq, state news agency reports indicated. The interception occurred at the Iraq border.

The incident highlights ongoing concerns about arms transfers in the region. Hezbollah, based in Lebanon, has long received support from Iran and allied forces in Syria and Iraq.

cards.headline: TSMC commits additional $100 billion to US chip production
cards.teaser: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company pledged another $100 billion for American facilities, raising its total US investment to $265 billion.
cards.body:
The BBC News source confirms the core facts of your original card, so here's a rewritten version:

TSMC has committed an additional $100 billion toward expanding semiconductor manufacturing in the United States, bringing its total pledged investment in American facilities to $265 billion. The investment is part of broader efforts to strengthen domestic chip production capacity and reduce reliance on overseas manufacturing.

The company stated the expansion will generate high-tech, high-paying employment opportunities in the US.

cards.headline: Eleven killed in fire at Algerian children's care home
cards.teaser: A fire at a care facility for children in Algeria left eleven people dead and nineteen injured.
cards.body:
Eleven people died in a fire at a children's care home in Algeria, with authorities confirming that nineteen others were injured in the blaze.

Algerian officials reported the fatalities and injuries at the facility, though details about what sparked the fire remain limited.

cards.headline: Pakistan resists UK efforts to deport grooming gang leader
cards.teaser: Pakistan's government says it has no connection to the deportation case of Shabir Ahmed, whom Britain is attempting to expel.
cards.body:
The government of Pakistan stated it has no connection whatsoever with the case of Shabir Ahmed, a grooming gang leader the United Kingdom is attempting to deport. The statement represents Pakistani resistance to UK deportation efforts.

Ahmed was convicted of leading a grooming gang in Britain. The case has become a diplomatic issue between the two countries as the UK seeks to remove him from British territory.

cards.headline: US military to screen troops for testosterone deficiency
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Hegseth authorized hormone screening for American service members to ensure they operate at peak performance.
cards.body:
Secretary of Defense Hegseth has authorized hormone screening for US military personnel to assess testosterone levels. According to Hegseth, the screening initiative is designed to ensure troops "operate at your absolute best."

The policy marks a new approach by the Pentagon to evaluating hormone levels among service members as part of military readiness efforts.

cards.headline: Pentagon removes bike lanes and speed cameras from safety best practices list
cards.teaser: The Federal Highway Administration quietly removed bike lanes and other safety measures from a key list of recommended practices, drawing criticism from safety advocates.
cards.body:
The Federal Highway Administration has removed bike lanes and speed cameras from its list of proven safety measures. The removals came from a key document outlining best practices for traffic safety that guides local transportation officials.

Safety advocates contend that bike lanes and automated enforcement cameras have documented records of reducing traffic crashes and deaths. Critics argue these measures represent proven strategies for improving road safety.

cards.headline: Hegseth orders annual testosterone screening for service members over 30
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth authorized hormone screening for military personnel, saying the tests will ensure troops operate at their best.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has authorized testosterone screening for military personnel over age 30. The policy aims to ensure service members "operate at your absolute best," according to Hegseth's announcement.

The mandatory hormone testing will be incorporated into military medical protocols as part of the initiative to screen for testosterone deficiency among older troops.

cards.headline: U.S. expands strikes into northern Iran and disables blockade-running ship
cards.teaser: American forces expanded military operations into northern Iran and stopped a ship attempting to breach a blockade.
cards.body:
The United States expanded its strikes into northern Iran as part of ongoing military operations in the region. American forces conducted attacks in areas beyond previous target zones.

U.S. forces also disabled a ship that attempted to run through a blockade. The vessel was stopped before it could breach the naval cordon. The operations represent an escalation in the geographic scope of American military action against Iran.

cards.headline: Ten unreleased David Bowie tracks from 1960s to be released
cards.teaser: Previously unheard recordings from David Bowie's early career will be released, featuring tracks recorded when he performed under the stage name Davie Jones.
cards.body:
Ten previously unheard recordings from David Bowie's early career will be released in a compilation called "David Bowie: The Shel Talmy Recordings." The tracks were recorded in 1965, when the artist performed under the stage name Davy Jones in London's vibrant mid-1960s music scene.

Some of the recordings feature guitarist Jimmy Page, before he joined Led Zeppelin. The material showcases Bowie's early blues-influenced pop-rock sound, distinct from the experimental work that would later define his career following hits like "Space Oddity" and the iconic "Ziggy Stardust" album.

cards.headline: UK Government Nationalizes British Steel to Secure Domestic Supply
cards.teaser: The British government has taken the Scunthorpe steelworks into public ownership, marking the nationalization of the country's last major steel mill.
cards.body:
The UK government has taken the Scunthorpe steelworks into public ownership under new powers passed this week. The facility represents Britain's last major steel mill and a critical part of the country's manufacturing infrastructure.

The government first stepped in last year when Chinese owner Jingye Group threatened to close the plant. With no private buyers coming forward, nationalization became the chosen path to preserve domestic steel production capacity and protect the thousands of jobs at the site.

cards.headline: US Diesel Prices Return to $5 Per Gallon
cards.teaser: Fuel costs have climbed 33% since the start of the Iran conflict as Persian Gulf fighting intensifies.
cards.body:
US diesel prices have climbed back above $5 per gallon for the second time this year, following their initial breach of that threshold in March. The resurgence reflects renewed military conflict in the Persian Gulf and constraints on domestic refining capacity.

The price surge has contributed to broader inflationary pressures. Diesel costs have risen 33% since the start of the Iran war, affecting transportation and shipping industries. Energy prices have been a major driver of inflation throughout the conflict, though a brief ceasefire in June provided temporary relief that helped cool the overall inflation rate to 3.5%.

cards.headline: UnitedHealth Raises Earnings Outlook After Cutting Costs
cards.teaser: The health insurance giant exceeded analyst estimates and increased its full-year profit forecast.
cards.body:
UnitedHealth Group reported second quarter earnings that surpassed Wall Street expectations and raised its outlook for the rest of the year. The company attributed the stronger performance to successful cost management initiatives.

The results signal continued recovery in UnitedHealth's Medicare Advantage business, which had faced pressure in recent quarters. The healthcare conglomerate's stock has been on a strong run as investors respond to improving fundamentals across its insurance and healthcare services divisions.

cards.headline: Aer Lingus Plans to Cut 500 Jobs in Cost-Saving Effort
cards.teaser: The Irish airline proposes eliminating positions across management, cabin crew, and pilots.
cards.body:
Aer Lingus has announced plans to eliminate 500 positions as part of a broader savings initiative. The proposed cuts include 290 roles in the airline's head office, 140 cabin crew positions, and 70 pilot jobs.

The restructuring reflects ongoing challenges facing European carriers as they balance operational costs with competitive pressures. The company has not detailed the timeline for implementing the job reductions or the total savings it expects to achieve through the workforce changes.

cards.headline: UK Economy Grew in May After April Contraction
cards.teaser: Modest expansion reversed a slight decline recorded in the previous month.
cards.body:
The United Kingdom economy returned to growth in May, reversing the slight contraction recorded in April. The expansion marked a turnaround in the country's economic trajectory after the previous month's decline.

The modest nature of the growth underscores the mixed economic conditions facing Britain as it navigates ongoing challenges to sustained expansion.

cards.headline: Consumer Regulator Investigates Petrol Station Parking Charges
cards.teaser: The inquiry targets potentially unfair practices by private parking operators at fuel stations.
cards.body:
British regulators have opened an investigation into parking charges imposed on drivers who queue at petrol stations. The probe focuses on fees collected by private parking operators who manage spaces at fuel retail locations.

The investigation forms part of a broader crackdown by the consumer regulator on potentially unfair parking practices. Officials are examining whether operators are applying charges inappropriately to drivers waiting to access fuel pumps during busy periods.

hero.headline: OnePlus exits US and European markets
hero.body:
OnePlus has officially confirmed it will stop releasing new smartphones in the United States and Europe, marking the end of the Chinese brand's presence in these major Western markets. The decision comes after years of industry speculation about the company's future direction in these regions.

The company, owned by parent firm Oppo, built its early reputation by offering high-end phone features at significantly lower prices than established competitors like Samsung and Apple. OnePlus launched in 2014 with an invitation-only sales model and quickly developed a devoted following among tech enthusiasts who appreciated what the brand called "flagship killer" devices. These phones delivered premium specifications and design at prices hundreds of dollars cheaper than traditional flagship models.

Over time, OnePlus expanded into physical retail stores and carrier partnerships, but the brand struggled to maintain its initial momentum as competition increased and pricing moved closer to mainstream flagship levels. The exit from the US and Europe represents a significant retreat for the smartphone maker.

The company also plans to wind down operations in India by 2027, which marks another substantial loss since India has been among OnePlus's strongest performing markets. This broader pullback is part of a larger restructuring within BBK Electronics, the parent company that also owns Vivo and Oppo. Sister brand Realme will simultaneously exit the Chinese market as part of the same reorganization.

Oppo has stated it will honor existing support and warranty agreements for current OnePlus customers in affected regions. The company plans to transition devices to ColorOS for future software updates and after-sale support. However, OnePlus has not provided detailed information about how warranty service will function or the timeline for software updates for existing US and European users.

The consolidation reflects broader industry trends as smartphone manufacturers face pressure from both premium competitors and budget-focused alternatives. In recent years, OnePlus and Oppo products have shown declining differentiation, with both brands sharing components, designs, and software features. By merging operations, Oppo can concentrate resources on its primary brand in markets where the two companies compete directly.

OnePlus devices are expected to remain available in China and other Asian markets where the brand maintains separate operations from Oppo. The withdrawal underscores how the global smartphone market has shifted since OnePlus's early days as a challenger brand. What once seemed like a disruptive force focused on value has become absorbed into larger corporate structures, leaving Western customers without a dedicated OnePlus presence going forward.

cards.headline: Google to allow third-party app stores on Android
cards.teaser: Google will permit rival app stores to operate within its Play Store starting next week, ending a legal dispute with Epic Games.
cards.body:
Google and Epic Games abandoned their settlement negotiations, clearing the way for third-party app stores to launch on Android devices. The change takes effect next week, allowing companies to distribute their own app marketplaces through the Google Play Store for the first time.

The decision follows Epic's legal victory over Google's app store practices. Google previously restricted competing app stores from easy distribution on Android, requiring users to enable security settings and manually install alternatives. The new policy removes these barriers, potentially reshaping how Android users discover and download applications.

cards.headline: Microsoft trains sales staff to position its AI models against OpenAI
cards.teaser: Microsoft is instructing salespeople to promote its in-house AI models as more efficient and cost-effective alternatives to OpenAI and Anthropic offerings.
cards.body:
Microsoft has begun training its sales teams to promote its own AI models over those from OpenAI and Anthropic. The company is positioning its in-house models as more efficient and cost-effective alternatives for enterprise customers.

This strategy marks a notable shift despite Microsoft's substantial $13 billion investment in OpenAI. While Microsoft continues to offer OpenAI's models through its Azure cloud platform, the sales guidance indicates the company is prioritizing its proprietary AI development for certain customer segments, reflecting intensifying competition among AI providers for enterprise business.

cards.headline: NASA rover photographs honeycomb-like patterns on Mars surface
cards.teaser: NASA's Curiosity rover captured images of unusual honeycomb-shaped formations on Mars, prompting scientific analysis of their origin.
cards.body:
NASA's Curiosity rover transmitted photographs showing honeycomb-pattern formations on the Martian surface. Scientists are examining the images to determine what geological processes created the distinctive hexagonal structures.

The patterns appear in rock formations photographed during the rover's exploration mission. Similar geometric patterns on Earth typically form through processes like mud cracking, salt crystallization, or volcanic cooling. Scientists will analyze the images alongside other geological data from the region to understand the formations' history and what they reveal about Mars' past environment.

cards.headline: Protesters rally at Bethesda headquarters over Xbox layoffs
cards.teaser: Hundreds gathered at Bethesda's offices to oppose Xbox layoffs and call for a return to contract negotiations with the union.
cards.body:
Hundreds of people demonstrated outside Bethesda's headquarters to protest recent Xbox layoffs and demand renewed contract talks. The union-organized rally aimed to halt what organizers described as a cycle of recurring job cuts at the gaming company.

The protest focused on getting management back to the bargaining table after negotiations stalled. Xbox has conducted multiple rounds of layoffs across its gaming studios in recent years, affecting developers at Bethesda and other acquired companies. Union representatives said the rally represented worker frustration with job insecurity in the gaming industry.

cards.headline: Skullcandy releases headphones incorporating Bose noise cancellation technology
cards.teaser: Skullcandy launched new wireless headphones featuring Bose active noise cancellation, marking the first collaboration between the two audio brands.
cards.body:
Skullcandy announced a new version of its Crusher wireless headphones featuring Bose's QuietControl active noise cancellation and head-tracking spatial audio technologies. The Crusher line is known for its dual-driver design in each ear cup—full-range and dedicated bass drivers—that enhance lower frequencies.

This collaboration marks a significant partnership between the two audio brands, combining Skullcandy's signature haptic bass feature with Bose's acclaimed noise cancellation technology in a single product.

cards.headline: New monkey species discovered in Democratic Republic of Congo
cards.teaser: Scientists identified a previously unknown monkey species with distinctive orange lips in a forest in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
cards.body:
Researchers have discovered a new monkey species in the forests of the Democratic Republic of Congo, distinguished by its striking orange-colored lips. Scientists describe the experience of encountering an animal so rarely known to exist as an amazing feeling.

The discovery highlights the remarkable biodiversity still being found in Central African forests. Despite extensive previous exploration of the region, these forests continue to reveal previously unknown species, adding to our understanding of primate diversity.

hero.headline: Red Bull to revert to conventional rear wing after Verstappen crashes
hero.body:
Red Bull Racing will revert to a conventional rear wing design for the Belgian Grand Prix following high-speed crashes involving Max Verstappen in the previous two races. The technical change represents a significant shift in the team's aerodynamic approach as it addresses concerns about stability.

The consecutive incidents prompted Red Bull's engineering team to reassess its current rear wing configuration. The team concluded that reverting to a more traditional wing setup would provide greater reliability and restore driver confidence in the car's behavior under racing conditions.

The Belgian Grand Prix at Spa-Francorchamps presents particular challenges due to the circuit's demanding high-speed corners. The track's nature means aerodynamic stability becomes crucial for both performance and safety. Managing downforce carefully through sections like Eau Rouge and Blanchimont requires precise balance. Red Bull's decision to switch wing designs suggests the team is prioritizing stability and consistency over the potential performance advantages of its experimental configuration.

The timing of this change matters significantly during the championship season. Verstappen has established himself as a dominant force in Formula 1 in recent years, and any technical adjustment could influence Red Bull's competitive standing. The team must ensure the conventional wing delivers sufficient performance to maintain their championship challenge while eliminating the risk factors that caused the recent accidents.

Red Bull has not provided specific details about what caused problems with the previous wing design or the exact circumstances of Verstappen's crashes. The team plans to evaluate the revised configuration during practice sessions at Spa before committing to it for qualifying and the race. How the wing change affects Red Bull's performance advantage will likely draw close attention from rival teams.

The decision comes as Red Bull has shown significant progress through recent races. Following upgrades at the Austrian Grand Prix, Verstappen finished second behind Mercedes' George Russell, demonstrating improved form despite experiencing a technical issue at the rear of the car during that race. Team principal Laurent Mekies expressed satisfaction with the team's trajectory, noting they had narrowed the gap to competitive rivals from more than a second away from winning pace at the season's start to within striking distance.

However, Verstappen has raised concerns about upcoming races under current Formula 1 regulations. After simulator work ahead of the British Grand Prix, he expressed skepticism about how the new engine formula would affect Silverstone's performance characteristics. The current regulations emphasize energy management with a roughly equal split between internal combustion engine power and the electrical battery and hybrid unit, which Verstappen and other drivers have criticized.

Despite these challenges, Lewis Hamilton acknowledged Red Bull's progress, highlighting how significantly the team had reduced the car's weight and developed strong upgrades. Mercedes, meanwhile, has demonstrated particular strength this season in energy recharging and electrical power deployment, suggesting they will be formidable competitors at Silverstone and beyond.

cards.headline: Lando Norris to receive 10-place grid penalty at Belgian Grand Prix
cards.teaser: McLaren driver faces grid drop after exceeding permitted engine component limits.
cards.body:
Lando Norris will receive a 10-place grid penalty at the Belgian Grand Prix after using more engine parts than regulations allow. The penalty will be applied to his qualifying position, moving him 10 places back on the starting grid.

Formula 1 limits the number of power unit components each driver can use during a season. Teams incur grid penalties when they exceed these allocations.

cards.headline: Scotland goalkeeper Craig Gordon announces retirement after 25-year career
cards.teaser: Veteran goalkeeper ends playing career spanning more than two decades.
cards.body:
Craig Gordon has announced his retirement from professional football, concluding a 25-year playing career. The Scotland international goalkeeper made the decision to step away from the game after a lengthy career at both club and international level.

Gordon represented Scotland at international level and played for several clubs during his career. His longevity as a professional goalkeeper spanned from the early 2000s through 2026, making him one of the longer-serving players of his generation. Gordon's retirement marks the end of an era for Scottish football.

cards.headline: Aston Villa close to signing Wolves midfielder Joao Gomes for 38 million pounds
cards.teaser: Portuguese midfielder set to depart relegated Wolves for Premier League side.
cards.body:
Joao Gomes is set to leave Wolverhampton Wanderers and join Aston Villa following Wolves' relegation from the Premier League. The transfer is valued at £38 million.

The midfielder will move to Villa as they strengthen their squad for the upcoming season.

cards.headline: England captain Harry Kane uncertain about playing at 2030 World Cup
cards.teaser: Striker says it is too early to decide whether he will continue international career.
cards.body:
Harry Kane says it is "too early" to judge whether he will continue playing for England until the 2030 World Cup. The captain made the comments following England's semi-final defeat to Argentina, when the team conceded two goals in the final minutes to lose 2-1.

Kane expressed his devastation over the loss, saying the entire squad and staff are gutted by the result. England had led 1-0 but Argentina equalized in the 85th minute through Enzo Fernández before Lautaro Martínez scored the winner in injury time. Kane noted how difficult it is to lose when the team came so close to reaching the final.

cards.headline: Argentina defender Cristian Romero calls Gary Neville criticism stupid
cards.teaser: Center-back responds to former England player's comments about defensive partnership.
cards.body:
Argentina defender Cristian Romero has criticized former England player Gary Neville for his analysis of the centre-back partnership between Romero and Lisandro Martinez. Romero labeled Neville's comments as "stupid" in response to the pundit's assessment of their defensive performance.

Neville, now working as a television pundit, had questioned aspects of how the pair played together during matches. The exchange reflects ongoing tension between players and former professionals who offer analysis and commentary on their performances.

cards.headline: Jude Bellingham slaps Argentina substitute after England World Cup exit
cards.teaser: England midfielder sparks melee following semi-final defeat to Argentina.
cards.body:
England's World Cup campaign ended in heartbreak when Argentina scored two late goals to win 2-1 in the semi-final in Atlanta. The defeat eliminated Thomas Tuchel's side from the tournament and prevented them from reaching the final.

In the immediate aftermath of the match, Jude Bellingham slapped Argentina substitute Valentin Barco on the back of the head, sparking a melee between players from both teams. The incident reflected the England midfielder's frustration following the dramatic loss.

hero.headline: Actor Sam Neill Died of Pneumonia, Agent Confirms
hero.body:
Actor Sam Neill Dies at 78

Sam Neill, the acclaimed New Zealand actor known for roles in Jurassic Park and The Piano, has died at age 78. He passed away Monday in Sydney, Australia, according to a statement shared on his Instagram account by his family.

Neill had recently revealed he was cancer-free following a diagnosis of stage three angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma, a type of blood cancer, in 2022. The family statement indicated his death was sudden and unexpected, noting that Neill remained cancer-free at the time of his passing. His family expressed gratitude to the staff at St Vincent's Private hospital for their care.

Neill was born Nigel John Dermot Neill in 1947 in Omagh, Northern Ireland, to an English mother and a New Zealand father serving in the British army. The family moved to New Zealand in 1954. He adopted the name Sam at age 12 because he felt it helped him move more easily through the world.

After initially studying law at Canterbury University, Neill turned to acting and joined the Downstage Theatre in Wellington as a professional actor. His breakout role came in 1977 with the film Sleeping Dogs, the first New Zealand film to open in the United States.

Neill's international career flourished throughout the 1980s and 1990s. He appeared in films including My Brilliant Career, Omen III, Possession, Evil Angels opposite Meryl Streep, and The Hunt for Red October. He gained widespread recognition in 1993 with two major roles: as settler Alisdair Stewart in Jane Campion's Oscar-winning film The Piano, and as Dr. Alan Grant in Steven Spielberg's Jurassic Park, a role originally offered to Harrison Ford. He reprised the role in two sequels.

Over five decades, Neill accumulated more than 150 credits in both film and television. His diverse filmography included Dead Calm, The Jungle Book, Event Horizon, and Bicentennial Man. In television, he played corrupt officer Maj Chester Campbell in the series Peaky Blinders and received a Golden Globe nomination for his portrayal of spy Sidney Reilly in 1983.

In 2016, Neill starred in Taika Waititi's hit film Hunt for the Wilderpeople, leading to cameo appearances in subsequent Thor films. He was considered a leading candidate to replace Roger Moore as James Bond and completed a screen test in 1986, though Timothy Dalton ultimately won the role.

Neill lived on a winery called Two Paddocks in Central Otago, New Zealand. In 2023, he revealed in his memoir Did I Ever Tell You This? that he had undergone chemotherapy for a year following his cancer diagnosis. By the time his book was published, his cancer had entered remission, though he continued monthly chemotherapy treatments for the rest of his life.

cards.headline: TikTok Faces Ofcom Investigation Over Child Age Checks
cards.teaser: The U.K. regulator opened an investigation into TikTok following a May review that criticized the platform's safety measures for children.
cards.body:
Ofcom has launched an investigation into TikTok's age verification systems following a May review that found the platform was not "safe enough" for children. The U.K. communications regulator will examine whether TikTok's current methods for checking users' ages meet required safety standards.

The investigation comes as Ofcom increases scrutiny of how platforms protect young people. The regulator has already taken action against other sites, including fining adult content websites for failing to prevent children from accessing their material.

cards.headline: Ten Unreleased David Bowie Tracks From 1960s to Be Released
cards.teaser: Previously unheard recordings from David Bowie's early career will be released, featuring material from when he performed under the name Davie Jones.
cards.body:
Ten previously unheard recordings from David Bowie's early career will be released in a compilation called David Bowie: The Shel Talmy Recordings. The tracks were recorded in 1965 when Bowie performed under the stage name Davy Jones, during his formative years in swinging 1960s London.

Some of the recordings feature guitarist Jimmy Page, before he formed Led Zeppelin. The material captures Bowie's early artistic direction—a sharp-suited artist playing blues-influenced pop-rock reminiscent of contemporaries like the Beatles, the Small Faces, and the Who. This predates his breakthrough with the 1969 hit Space Oddity and his later transformation into a rock icon.

cards.headline: Author Arundhati Roy Discusses Beatles Songs and AI at London Indian Film Festival
cards.teaser: The Booker Prize winner spoke about unauthorized Beatles music in a restored 1980s film and the role of artificial intelligence in modern cinema.
cards.body:
Arundhati Roy discussed the unauthorized use of Beatles songs in the film In Which Annie Gives It Those Ones during a question-and-answer session at BFI Southbank following the U.K. premiere of the film's 4K restoration. Roy also addressed the growing presence of artificial intelligence in cinema and the handmade aesthetic of independent filmmaking.

The event took place at the London Indian Film Festival. Roy won the Booker Prize for her novel The God of Small Things. The restored film dates from the 1980s and has been remastered in 4K resolution.

cards.headline: Celebrity Influencers Paid Up to £1 Million to Advertise Deodorant on Instagram
cards.teaser: The chief executive of Wild revealed payment details for social media advertising campaigns featuring celebrity endorsements.
cards.body:
Celebrity influencers received payments of up to £1 million to advertise deodorant products on Instagram, according to the chief executive of Wild. The company's leader discussed what happens behind the scenes of social media advertising posts.

The disclosure provides insight into the commercial side of influencer marketing and the substantial sums paid to celebrities for product endorsements on social media platforms. Wild manufactures personal care products and has used celebrity partnerships as part of its marketing strategy.

cards.headline: Eric Stonestreet Says Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce Created Normalcy at Wedding
cards.teaser: The actor commented on the couple's wedding at Madison Square Garden, describing the security arrangements that allowed them privacy.
cards.body:
Eric Stonestreet said Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce created the normalcy they deserve at their wedding, which took place at Madison Square Garden. The actor noted that security arrangements allowed the couple to have a private evening while keeping everyone safe.

Stonestreet attended the wedding at the New York venue. The security measures enabled Swift and Kelce to enjoy the event away from public attention despite their high-profile status.

cards.headline: Cricket Dominated India's Streaming Viewership in First Half of 2026
cards.teaser: The ICC Men's T20 World Cup and Indian Premier League drew the most viewers on streaming platforms, according to a new report.
cards.body:
Cricket properties dominated streaming viewership in India during the first half of 2026, according to Ormax Media's Ormax StreamView report. The ICC Men's T20 World Cup drew an estimated 246 million viewers on JioHotstar between January and June, more than any other tracked title.

The Indian Premier League 2026, also streamed on JioHotstar, recorded 228.4 million viewers during the same period. Both cricket tournaments significantly outpaced other content in the measurement framework for streaming viewership in India.

hero.headline: Todd Blanche faces confirmation hearing for attorney general
hero.teaser: President Trump's nominee to lead the Justice Department answered questions from lawmakers about his relationship with Trump and potential investigations.
hero.body:
Todd Blanche appeared before the Senate Judiciary Committee on Wednesday for his confirmation hearing as President Trump's nominee to lead the Justice Department. The hearing revealed significant tensions as lawmakers from both parties questioned his close relationship with Trump and his role in the administration's recent decisions.

Blanche, who previously served as Trump's personal attorney and later as deputy attorney general, sought to distance himself from his close ties to the president. When asked directly by Louisiana Senator John Kennedy whether the two men were friends, Blanche initially said "I'm his lawyer" before correcting himself to "Was his lawyer." He later emphasized that his role as Trump's counsel did not make him a "yes man," and he claimed to have disagreed with the president on occasions, including on whether Trump was eligible to run for a third term.

The hearing focused on several controversial matters. Blanche faced pointed questioning about a settlement agreement between the Justice Department and Trump over a $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS. The deal included a $1.8 billion fund intended to compensate victims of alleged government weaponization, though Blanche acknowledged the term was not specifically defined. The agreement also granted Trump, his family, and his businesses immunity from tax audits. A federal judge on Monday criticized the arrangement as collusive. Facing bipartisan backlash, Blanche scrapped the fund.

Republican Senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis, both critical of the settlement, pressed Blanche during the hearing. Cornyn remained "undecided" on the nomination, while Tillis seemed to warm to Blanche after he stated that anyone who harmed law enforcement on January 6 should have been prosecuted. Tillis told Blanche he had done a good job.

Democratic Senator Dick Durbin raised concerns about the Justice Department's handling of files related to Jeffrey Epstein. Blanche acknowledged that the release contained "mistakes," including redaction errors. He defended the department's conduct but said he could not directly meet with Epstein survivors if they were represented by attorneys, though his staff would do so.

When asked by Democratic Senator Amy Klobuchar about whether armed agents would be deployed to polls in November, Blanche said he would "absolutely commit to following the law" but did not directly address the concern.

Blanche also defended FBI Director Kash Patel against reports about his drinking habits and use of the FBI's airplane. "I don't think he has any issues drinking," Blanche said. "I don't think there's any issues with morale there."

The confirmation faces a tight margin. Blanche cannot afford to lose a single Republican vote on the committee for his nomination to advance. Democratic Senator Cory Booker of New Jersey has publicly stated his opposition to the nomination.

cards.headline: Trump reverses DHS pause on ICE vehicle stops after two fatal shootings
cards.teaser: President Trump reversed a Department of Homeland Security decision to pause certain ICE vehicle stops, overruling his own agency after becoming angry about the.
cards.body:
President Trump reversed a Department of Homeland Security decision to pause certain ICE vehicle stops, overruling his own agency after becoming angry about the temporary measure. The DHS had announced the pause following two fatal shootings by ICE agents in recent weeks, with the intent to provide additional training to agents before resuming such operations.

Late Tuesday at the White House, Trump complained to advisers about the pause, according to reports. By Wednesday morning, he posted on Truth Social reversing the decision, leaving DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin and border czar Tom Homan to explain the abrupt change in policy.

The two fatal shootings that prompted the original pause involved immigrant fathers who were killed during ICE operations. Federal immigration agents involved in the recent shootings were not wearing body cameras, according to the agency. The DHS had earlier pledged to equip all immigration agents with body cameras, but months later that promise has not been fulfilled.

The reversal highlights tension between the White House and DHS over immigration enforcement operations. The original pause was intended as a temporary safety measure while agents received additional training on vehicle stop procedures. Trump's intervention means ICE agents will continue conducting vehicle stops without the planned training period.

The episode demonstrates how the recent fatal shootings have created pressure on the administration's immigration enforcement policies. The lack of body camera footage from either incident has made it difficult to establish complete accounts of what occurred during the confrontations that led to the deaths.

cards.headline: Trump to address nation as political pressures mount
cards.teaser: The president plans an evening address as polling shows public opposition to renewed military action against Iran.
cards.body:
President Trump will address the nation Thursday evening as his administration faces multiple political challenges. A new Economist/YouGov poll shows 65 percent of Americans want an immediate deal to end the conflict with Iran, which Trump recently restarted.

The war on Iran has been unpopular since it began. Trump's decision to resume military action has intensified criticism as he prepares for the speech, which will be delivered from the White House.

cards.headline: House Republicans struggle with $95 billion budget package
cards.teaser: GOP leaders face pressure from the calendar and their own members over a reconciliation framework set for committee action.
cards.body:
House Republican leaders are working against time constraints and internal opposition as they prepare to advance a $95 billion reconciliation framework through the Budget Committee. The package faces questions about whether it can pass the House and reach President Trump's desk.

The budget proposal has generated frustration among Republican members, creating uncertainty about its prospects. GOP leaders scheduled the Budget Committee action for Thursday despite concerns from within their own caucus about the framework's contents and scope.

cards.headline: TV networks weigh decision on airing Trump speech
cards.teaser: Broadcasters face editorial judgment about carrying presidential address focused on elections.
cards.body:
Television networks are deciding whether to carry President Trump's primetime address scheduled for 9 p.m. ET from the East Room. Trump said the speech will focus on free and fair elections and promised a very big announcement.

The decision has become a high-stakes editorial judgment for broadcast networks. Networks must weigh the risk of airing potential falsehoods about the 2020 election against backlash from a White House that has shown willingness to confront media outlets.

cards.headline: South Carolina GOP Senate primary has no clear frontrunner
cards.teaser: Multiple candidates vie to replace Senator Lindsey Graham, who died at age 71 while seeking a fifth term.
cards.body:
A new poll shows no leading candidate in the Republican primary to replace Senator Lindsey Graham of South Carolina. Graham was seeking his fifth Senate term when he died.

The GOP primary field remains crowded, with multiple candidates competing for the seat without an obvious frontrunner emerging from the race.

cards.headline: Vice President Vance takes media offensive
cards.teaser: Vance appears on outlets outside conservative media to defend White House policies.
cards.body:
Vice President Vance is appearing on media outlets beyond conservative channels to defend the administration against critics. The approach mirrors the strategy that helped him secure Trump's vice presidential selection.

Vance is using the interviews to demonstrate his skill in verbal confrontations while building support for an expected 2028 presidential campaign. His willingness to engage with outlets beyond Fox News and Newsmax contrasts with other prominent administration officials who limit their media appearances to conservative channels.
